newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end lower on milder weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end lower on milder weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished lower Wednesday amid forecasts of weather in parts of the western U.S. turning milder next week after a recent heatwave, brokers and traders said.
"It was a big break in the weather and the three-day weekend," said James Fiedler, senior vice-president at E.D.& F. Man International Futures Inc., referring to the U.S. Labor Day holiday weekend.
Meanwhile, softer western natural gas prices and restoration of two transmission power lines in southern California also pressured futures and physcial prices lower, marketers said.
October California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled down 29 cents at $16.11 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trading between $16.00 and $16.35.
November COB ended at $16.85, down 25 cents from Tuesday's settlement. Deferred COB months finished mixed, with summer 1997 contracts closing 10 to 75 cents higher.
October Palo Verde (PV) futures settled down 30 cents at $16.50 per MWh after moving in a tight 10 cent range.
November PV ended down 20 cents at $15.65. Outer-month PV contracts finished 10 to 30 cents lower.
Brokers and traders expect the electricity complex to test lower levels Thursday.
"The main trend is still down," Fiedler said.
NYMEX estimated 120 COB and 77 PV contracts were sold Wednesday.
